Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so we all have the same view:

- Goals we heard: improve customer support summarization accuracy, keep 95th pct latency under ~250ms for interactive UI, and do a 2-week PoC against a representative prompt set.
- Constraints: PII must remain in-region (US), and you prefer tooling that can show regressions by prompt slice.

Recommended next steps:
1) I attached our initial benchmark CSV and Redwood-verified performance profiles PDF for the recommended model variants.
2) Start a small PoC using either the hosted API or Dedicated (we can provision a 1-GPU reserved pool).
3) We’ll run your prompt set through Redwood’s eval harness and produce quality/latency regression reports. Please find an initial sample prompt set attached (acme_prompt_set-v1.txt) — you can swap in your production set for the PoC.

Model recommendations from the call (based on your quality vs cost tradeoffs):
- r4-q8_0 (Redwood-4x-quantized): Best cost/throughput balance for 8–16k context. Good for production with prefix caching.
- OpenLlama-3-13B (fp16): Slightly higher latency but better generative quality on long-form prompts.

I’ve also included links to the Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS and latency percentiles) and a shared Drive with full benchmark artifacts. The attached CSV includes per-workload TPS and 50/95/99 latency percentiles we measured on A100 and T4 testbeds.

Next step: Can we schedule a 30-min PoC kickoff early next week? I’ll bring Marissa for the eval plan and Dylan for the infra/cost estimates.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez

Laura — great questions. Short answers and attached artifacts below.

1) TPS / latency numbers (summary):
- r4-q8_0 on NVIDIA A100 (private Redwood test harness, 1024-context, mixed unigram prompt mix similar to customer traffic): 85 TPS sustained, 95th pct latency = 210ms, 99th pct = 320ms. These were measured with continuous batching and prefix KV caching enabled.
- r4-q8_0 on T4 (edge test): ~28 TPS, 95th pct latency = 480ms.
- OpenLlama-3-13B (fp16) on A100: ~45 TPS, 95th pct latency = 300ms.

Notes: the numbers above are for our standard eval harness. We include percentiles (50/95/99) in the attached CSV (acme_benchmark_results.csv) and a condensed Redwood-verified profile (redwood_performance_profiles.pdf) showing how throughput changes with batch size and sequence length. Link: https://app.redwood.ai/perf-profiles#r4-q8_0

2) Workload fidelity:
- The standard harness uses a customer-mix mode (real prompt distributions with multi-turn context and variance in response length). We ran a subset of the CSV workloads using a noisy multi-turn history generator to mirror your described traffic pattern. I’ve marked those rows in the CSV. For PoC we’ll run your exact prompt set end-to-end to produce apples-to-apples numbers.

3) Quality/regression detection:
- We recommend a prompt slice suite with three buckets: critical slices (billing/cancellation flows), user-facing summaries (the UI path you highlighted), and long-form multi-turn threads. I attached acme_prompt_set-v1.txt as a starter.
- Redwood’s eval tooling produces per-slice ROUGE/BLEU-style scores (custom metrics) and A/B comparison diffs. We can wire up automated alerts for quality regressions on rollout (e.g., revert if average score drops >2 points on critical slices).

Next steps / PoC plan:
- Day 0: Provision PoC env (hosted or dedicated) and upload your full prompt set.
- Week 1: Run throughput/latency sweep and initial quality eval.
- Week 2: Iterate on model variant or quantization profile and produce final recommendations + cost delta.

Estimated sample cost for a 2-week PoC (hosted, using r4-q8_0 at scale equivalent to 1 A100 sustained test harness): $3.5k–$6k (depends on traffic rate and data retention choices). If you want dedicated reserved capacity pricing, I’ll have Dylan provide a committed monthly estimate.

Attachments: acme_benchmark_results.csv, redwood_performance_profiles.pdf, acme_prompt_set-v1.txt

Let me know which day next week works for the kickoff — Tue/Wed morning PST are open.

Thanks,
Alex
